It was the first of three major Paleozoic orogenies responsible for the formation of the Appalachian Mountains. The **Taconic Mountains**, also known as the **Taconics**, are a mountain range in the northeastern United States, running along the eastern border of New York State and the western borders of Massachusetts and Vermont. A small portion also extends into northwestern Connecticut. They are part of the Appalachian Mountains, though geologically distinct, characterized by their heavily eroded, rounded peaks and mature forest cover.. The highest point in the range is generally considered to be Mount Frissell (2,454 feet or 748 meters), whose western slope holds the highest point in Connecticut. The range extends approximately 150 miles (240 km) from north to south..
